about: The first part of text ga, the bardo of the wrathful deities. After the seven days of the peaceful deities, each of them a narrow passage at which the dead were pointed out and many freed, the text explains why many still are not: beings are countless, their karma and habits strong, and the wheel of ignorance never runs down. Now the fifty-eight blazing blood-drinking wrathful deities dawn, which are the peaceful deities changed in form, and terror makes recognition harder, though it also holds the mind to one point, so that a little recognition frees. Learning does not help here: abbots who hold the monastic discipline and teachers of philosophy, who never took the secret mantra to heart or who disparaged it, do not recognise its deities and turn from them in hatred, which is why no relics or rainbow light appear when they die. A follower of the secret mantra, even the lowest, even of unseemly conduct, recognises the wrathful deities as his own yidam and is freed, and signs appear at his death; practitioners of middling ability and above are led to the Sky-Faring realm as their breath stops, with a clear sky, rainbow light, flowers, scent and music for signs. Great meditators of the Great Perfection and the Great Seal recognise the clear light at the moment of death and need no reading; others attain the three bodies in the three bardos or are born in the higher realms. The part closes with praise of the Great Liberation through Hearing as the teaching that frees by hearing alone, after which no being it has reached can go to the lower realms.

sentences.w: ཁྲོ་བོའི་ བར་དོ་ འཆར་ཚུལ་ བསྟན་པ་ བཞུགས་སོ༔
sentences.l: Wrathful-ones' between, dawning-manner showing, is-here.
sentences.i: Here is the showing of how the bardo of the wrathful deities dawns.
sentences.n: The title leaf of text ga, the third text of the volume and the second part of the Great Liberation through Hearing; the letter ga stands in the top margin. Like the title of text kha in the pilot, it is one phrase closed by bzhugs so, 'is present', the respectful way a title page says 'here is'. khro bo, 'wrathful one' (khro, 'wrath'), the wrathful forms of the deities, against the zhi ba, 'peaceful', of the parts before. 'char tshul, 'the way of dawning' (tshul, 'manner, way'); bstan pa, 'showing, teaching', the past stem of ston, 'to show', made a noun with -pa. The print runs bar do and 'char together with no tsheg (བར་དོའཆར), here divided; it does the same in the next line.

sentences.w: ད་ ནི་ ཁྲོ་བོའི་ བར་དོ་ འཆར་ཚུལ་ བསྟན་པར་ བྱ་ སྟེ༔
sentences.l: Now, as-for, wrathful-ones' between, dawning-manner showing-to is-to-be-done, and:
sentences.i: Now the way the bardo of the wrathful deities dawns will be shown.
sentences.n: The opening words repeat the title. bstan par bya, 'is to be shown': bya, the future stem of byed, 'to do', after a verb with -r means 'is to be done, will be done'. ste, 'and', links the clause to what follows; it takes the form te or de after some final letters (the clause chain, as in the parts before). The print again runs bar do and 'char together.

sentences.w: དེ་ ཡང་ གོང་དུ་ ཞི་བའི་ བར་དོ་ ལ་ འཕྲང་ རིམ་པ་ བདུན་ ཡོད་ དེ༔
sentences.l: That also: above, peaceful's between in, narrow-passages stages seven there-are, and:
sentences.i: In the peaceful bardo above there were seven narrow passages, one after another,
sentences.n: de yang, 'that, too', opens an explanation, 'now, ...'. gong du, 'above', means earlier in the text: the seven days of the peaceful deities, parts 003 to 008. 'phrang, 'narrow passage, defile', a dangerous place on a road; each day was one such passage. rim pa, 'stage, step, in order'. yod de, 'there are, and': de is the form of ste after -d.

sentences.w: དེ་ ལ་ རིམ་པ་ བཞིན་དུ་ ངོ་སྤྲད་པས༔ ཅིག་ ལ་ མ་ འཕྲོད་ ཀྱང་ གཅིག་ ལ་ འཕྲོད་ དེ་ གྲོལ་བ་ ཐོབ་པ་ ནི་ དཔག་ཏུ་མེད་པར་ འབྱུང་ངོ་༔
sentences.l: Them-at, stages according-to, face-introduced-because: one at not met though, one at met, and, freedom obtaining, as-for, measure-to without-ly arises.
sentences.i: and because the dead were pointed out at each in turn, those who did not recognise at one recognised at another and were freed; those who gained freedom so are beyond counting.
sentences.n: The print has དེ་ཡ (de ya), a misprint for དེ་ལ (de la), corrected here: the letter was compared with other ya and la on the page, and only de la, 'at them, to them', gives sense; the reading is fairly but not wholly sure. rim pa bzhin du, 'stage by stage, in order'. ngo sprad pas, 'because they were pointed out' (ngo sprad, the past of ngo sprod, 'point out', with -pa and -s 'by, because'). ngo and thob are both doubtful on the image ([?]): a naro may be hidden under the line above, which would give other letters; ngo sprad and thob pa are the words the sense needs. cig la ma 'phrod kyang gcig la 'phrod, 'though it is not met at one, it is met at another': ngo 'phrod, 'the face meets', is recognition; cig and gcig, 'one', are the same word in two spellings. The print writes la ma as one sign at the line end (ལམ), and runs la and 'phrod together at the next line join; both are written out here. dpag tu med par 'byung, 'arise beyond measure'; 'byung ngo, with the sentence-ending -o repeated after -ng.

sentences.w: དེ་ལྟར་ གྲོལ་བ་ མང་དུ་ བྱུང་ ཡང་༔ སེམས་ཅན་ ནི་ གྲངས་ མང་༔ ལས་ངན་ ནི་ ཚན་ཆེ༔ སྡིག་སྒྲིབ་ ནི་ ལྷུན་སྟུག༔ བག་ཆགས་ ནི་ ཡུན་རིང༔ མ་རིག་ འཁྲུལ་འཁོར་ འདི་ ལ་ ཟད་པ་ མེད་ ཅིང་ འཕྲི་བ་ ལ་ མེད་པས༔
sentences.l: Thus freedom many-ly arose though: beings, as-for, numbers many; bad-deeds, as-for, force great; wrongs-obscurations, as-for, dense-thick; habitual-tendencies, as-for, duration long; ignorance's delusion-wheel this at, exhausting is-not and, lessening at(?) is-not, because:
sentences.i: Yet though many were freed in this way, beings are countless, bad karma is strong, wrongdoing and obscuration are thick, habitual tendencies are long-standing, and this delusive wheel of ignorance never runs out and never grows less. So
sentences.n: Four short clauses, each with ni, 'as for', set out why so many remain: sems can ni grangs mang, 'beings, their numbers are many'; las ngan ni tshan che, 'bad karma, its force is great' (tshan che, 'strong'); sdig sgrib ni lhun stug, 'wrongs and obscurations are dense' (sdig, 'wrongdoing'; sgrib, 'obscuration'; lhun stug, 'massive, thick'); bag chags ni yun ring, 'habitual tendencies are of long duration'. The print sets the ༔ after stug and ring apart from the word, with no tsheg. mang du[?] byung: on the image one u-loop serves both du and the bya below it, so du is not sure. byung is the past stem, 'arose, have been', where the other recension has the present 'byung. ma rig 'khrul 'khor: 'khrul 'khor is a machine or turning device, and it carries both 'khrul, 'delusion', and 'khor, 'turning, saṃsāra': 'the delusive wheel of ignorance'. zad pa med, 'there is no running out'; 'phri ba la[?] med, 'there is no lessening': the la is doubtful, is not in the other recension, and makes the phrase awkward; it is translated as if absent. med pas, 'because there is not', runs on into the next sentence.

sentences.w: དེ་ལྟར་ ཞིབ་ཏུ་ ངོ་སྤྲད་ ཀྱང་ མ་ གྲོལ་བར་ ཐུར་དུ་ འཁྱམས་པ་ ཡང་ ཚན་ཆེ་ སྟེ༔
sentences.l: Thus in-detail face-introduced though, not freed-ly, downward wandering also force great, and:
sentences.i: even when they are pointed out so carefully, many are not freed and wander downward.
sentences.n: zhib tu, 'in detail, carefully'. ngo sprad kyang, 'though pointed out': the other recension has cing, 'pointed out, and', which loses the 'even though'; the print is followed. ma grol bar, 'without being freed'. thur du, 'downward', toward the lower births. tshan che, 'great in force', as in the sentence before, is here taken as 'are many, prevail': those who wander down are also a great number.

sentences.w: དེ་ ཡང་ ཞི་བའི་ ལྷ་ཚོགས་ དང་༔ རིག་འཛིན་ མཁའ་འགྲོའི་ ལྷ་ཚོགས་ ཀྱི་ བསུ་བ་ འདས་པའི་ འོག་ཏུ་ ཁྲག་འཐུང་ ཁྲོ་བོའི་ ལྷ་ཚོགས་ འབར་བ་ ལྔ་བཅུ་རྩ་བརྒྱད༔ གོང་ གི་ ཞི་བའི་ ལྷ་ཚོགས་ གནས་ བསྒྱུར་ དེ་ འཆར་དུ་ འོང་བས་ གོང་ དང་ མི་ འདྲ་ སྟེ༔
sentences.l: That also: peaceful's deity-host and; knowledge-holders sky-goers' deity-host's welcoming passed's after-at, blood-drinking wrathful-ones' deity-host blazing fifty-and-eight; above's peaceful's deity-host, state transformed, and(?), dawning come-because, above with not alike, and:
sentences.i: After the welcome of the hosts of peaceful deities and of the knowledge-holders and sky-goers has passed, the fifty-eight blazing blood-drinking wrathful deities come. They are the peaceful deities of before, changed in state, who now dawn, and so they are not like what went before.
sentences.n: khrag 'thung, 'blood-drinker' (khrag, 'blood'; 'thung, 'to drink'; Sanskrit heruka), the name of the wrathful deities; 'bar ba, 'blazing'. lnga bcu rtsa brgyad, 'fifty-eight': lnga bcu, 'fifty', and rtsa, which joins the units to the tens, brgyad, 'eight'. bsu ba 'das pa'i 'og tu, 'after the welcoming has passed': the knowledge-holders and sky-goers came to welcome the dead in 007 and 008. The other recension has bsun ma 'das, which differs. 'dzin[?] in rig 'dzin is squeezed against the frame on the image and not sure, but the word is the one the sense needs; the print runs it and mkha' together with no tsheg, here divided. gnas bsgyur, 'changed in state' (gnas, 'place, state'; bsgyur, the past stem of sgyur, 'to change, transform'), where the other recension has gnas 'gyur nas, 'having changed'. de after bsgyur is taken as the clause link 'and', though after -r it is usually written te; it could also be 'that'. 'char du 'ong, 'come to dawn'; -bas, 'because'. gong dang mi 'dra, 'not like before': dang, 'with', after 'dra, 'to be alike'. The other recension ends the sentence at 'ong ngo and goes on with da ni ... 'dir.

sentences.w: འདི་ ནི་ ཁྲོ་བོའི་ བར་དོ་ ཡིན་པས༔ འཇིགས་ སྐྲག་ དངངས་ གསུམ་ གྱི་ དབང་དུ་ འགྲོ་ སྟེ༔ ངོ་ འཕྲོད་པ་ ཡང་ དཀའ་རུ་ འགྲོའོ༔
sentences.l: This, as-for, wrathful-ones' between is-because: fear, fright, terror, three's power-into go, and: face-meeting also difficult-ly goes.
sentences.i: Because this is the bardo of the wrathful deities, the dead fall into the power of fear, fright and terror, and recognition grows harder.
sentences.n: 'jigs skrag dngangs gsum, 'the three, fear, fright and terror', three words for one thing, said again below as dngangs skrag 'jigs gsum; dngangs is the print's spelling of sngangs, 'to be terrified'. dbang du 'gro, 'go into the power (of)'. dka' ru 'gro, 'go to difficulty, become hard': ru, 'to, into', after a word ending in a vowel; 'gro'o, 'goes', with the sentence-ending -'o after a vowel. The print runs 'di and ni together at the page end (འདིནི) and ni and khro across the page join; here divided.

sentences.w: རིག་པ་ རང་དབང་ མི་ ཐོབ་ བརྒྱལ་བ་ ཁོར་ཡུག་ཏུ་ འོང་ སྟེ༔
sentences.l: Knowing own-power not obtains, fainting circle-whole-ly comes, and:
sentences.i: Awareness gets no command of itself, and fainting comes over it again and again;
sentences.n: The print has བརྒྱལ་བབཁོར (brgyal ba ba khor, the second ba with no tsheg), a misprint for བརྒྱལ་བ་ཁོར (brgyal ba khor), corrected here: the letter ba is set twice, once as the last syllable of brgyal ba, 'fainting, swoon', and again before khor; the correction is fairly but not wholly sure. rang dbang, 'own power, control of oneself'; mi thob, 'does not get', with mi, the 'not' of the present. khor yug tu, 'all round, without a break' (khor yug, 'circumference, the whole round'); the sense, swoon upon swoon, is taken from the words and is not sure. The print also runs thob and brgyal together at the line join, here divided.

sentences.w: ཅུང་ཟད་ ཅིག་ ངོས་ ཟིན་ ནས་ གྲོལ་བར་ སླ་ སྟེ༔
sentences.l: A-little one recognition caught, then, freed-as easy, and:
sentences.i: yet if one recognises even a little, freedom is easy.
sentences.n: cung zad cig, 'a little'. ngos zin, 'the face is caught', to recognise, as in the parts before. grol bar sla, 'it is easy to be freed': sla, 'easy', with the verb in -r before it. The other recension has grol bar yang sla, 'it is also easy'; the print has no yang.

sentences.w: དེ་ ཅིའི་ ཕྱིར་ ཞེ་ ན༔ དངངས་ སྐྲག་ འཇིགས་ གསུམ་ གྱི་ སྣང་བ་ ཤར་བས༔ རིག་པ་ ཡེངས་ ལོངས་ མེད་ དེ༔ རིག་པ་ རྩེ་གཅིག་ཏུ་ བསྒྲིམས་ ནས་ ཡོད་པའི་ ཕྱིར༔
sentences.l: That why, if-one-says: terror, fright, fear, three's appearances dawned-because, knowing distraction leisure is-not, and: knowing one-pointedly concentrated, then, being's because.
sentences.i: Why is that? Because the appearances of terror, fright and fear have dawned, awareness has no leisure to wander; it stays drawn together to a single point.
sentences.n: de ci'i phyir zhe na, 'if one says, why is that?', the usual way the text puts a question to itself: ci'i phyir, 'for the sake of what, why'; zhe na, 'if one says' (zhe, a form of zhes). yengs longs med, 'there is no leisure for distraction' (yengs, 'to be distracted'; longs, 'leisure, room'). rtse gcig tu, 'one-pointedly'; bsgrims, 'drawn tight, concentrated', the past stem of sgrim; nas yod, 'is, having been', the state that follows. phyir at the end, 'because', answers the question.

sentences.w: འདིའི་ སྐབས་སུ༔ འདི་ ལྟ་བུའི་ གདམས་པ་ དང་ མ་ འཕྲད་ ན༔ ཐོས་པ་ རྒྱ་མཚོ་ ལྟ་བུ་ ཡོད་ ཀྱང་ འདིར་ ཕན་པ་ མེད་ དེ༔
sentences.l: This's occasion-at: this like's instruction with not met if, hearing ocean like there-is though, here benefit is-not, and:
sentences.i: At this point, if one has not met with an instruction like this, even learning as vast as the ocean is of no help here.
sentences.n: 'di'i skabs su, 'at this juncture'. 'phrad, 'to meet', takes dang, 'with', for what is met. ma ... na, 'if not', the pattern of the pilot. thos pa, 'hearing', is learning, what one has heard from teachers; rgya mtsho lta bu, 'like an ocean'. phan pa med, 'there is no benefit'.

sentences.w: འདུལ་བ་ འཛིན་པའི་ མཁན་པོ་ དང་༔ མཚན་ཉིད་ ཀྱི་ སྟོན་པ་ ཆེན་པོ་ རྣམས་ ཀྱང་༔ སྐབས་ འདིར་ འཁྲུལ་ ནས་ ངོ་ མ་ འཕྲོད་ དེ༔ འཁོར་བར་ འཁྱམས་པ་ ཡོད་དོ༔
sentences.l: Discipline holding's abbots and; characteristics' teachers great (plural) also: occasion this-at, deluded, then, face not meeting, and: in-saṃsāra wandering there-is.
sentences.i: Even abbots who hold the monastic discipline and great teachers of philosophy go astray at this point, do not recognise, and wander in saṃsāra.
sentences.n: 'dul ba, 'discipline' (Sanskrit vinaya), the monastic code; 'dul ba 'dzin pa, 'one who holds the discipline'; mkhan po, 'abbot', the senior monk who gives ordination. mtshan nyid, 'defining characteristic', is the name for the study of philosophy by definitions and debate; mtshan nyid kyi ston pa, 'a teacher of philosophy'. The two stand for learned monks who have not practised the tantras, and come four times in this part. 'khrul nas, 'having gone astray, deluded'. 'khor bar, 'in saṃsāra', 'khor ba with -r. 'khyams pa yod do, 'there are (those) who wander'.

sentences.w: སྐྱེ་བོ་ ཐ་མལ་པ་ རྣམས་ ནི་ ཧ་ཅང་ ཡང་ ཆེ་ སྟེ༔ དངངས་ སྐྲག་ འཇིགས་ གསུམ་ ལ་ བྲོས་པས་ ངན་སོང་ གི་ གཡང་ ལ་ ལྷུང་ ནས་ སྡུག་བསྔལ་ལོ༔
sentences.l: People ordinary (plural), as-for, exceedingly even great, and: terror, fright, fear, three from fled-because, bad-destinies' abyss into falling, then, suffer.
sentences.i: For ordinary people it is far worse: fleeing from terror, fright and fear, they fall over the precipice into the lower realms and suffer.
sentences.n: skye bo tha mal pa, 'ordinary people'. ha cang yang che, 'is even greater, far too great': ha cang, 'too, exceedingly'; yang, 'even'; the wandering is meant. bros pas, 'because they flee'; la, 'from' with bros. ngan song, 'bad going', the three lower realms of hell-beings, hungry ghosts and animals (into-bad-destinies in the literal line, as in 002). g.yang, 'abyss, precipice', here without the -sa of the usual g.yang sa. sdug bsngal lo, 'they suffer', the sentence-ending -lo after -l.

sentences.w: གསང་སྔགས་ ལ་ སྤྱོད་པའི་ རྣལ་འབྱོར་པ་ ཐ་མའི་ ཡང་ ཐ་མ་ ཅིག་ ཡིན་ ན་ ཡང་༔ ཁྲག་འཐུང་ གི་ ལྷ་ཚོགས་ མཐོང་ མ་ཐག་ཏུ་ སྔར་འདྲིས་ ཀྱི་ མི་ དང་ འཕྲད་པ་ ལྟ་བུ་ ཡི་དམ་ གྱི་ ལྷ་ ཡིན་པར་ ངོ་ ཤེས༔ ཡིད་ཆེས་ ཏེ་ གཉིས་སུ་ མེད་པར་ ཐིམ་ ནས་ སངས་རྒྱས་པར་ འགྱུར་རོ༔
sentences.l: Secret-mantra in practising's yogin, lowest's even lowest one is if even: blood-drinkers' deity-host seen as-soon-as, before acquainted's person with meeting like, yidam's deity being-as face knows; trusting, and, two-as without-ly dissolving, then, buddha-ly becomes.
sentences.i: But a yogin who practises the secret mantra, even the lowest of the low, as soon as he sees the hosts of blood-drinking deities, knows them for the deities of his yidam, as one meets a person one knew before; he trusts them, dissolves into them without duality, and becomes a buddha.
sentences.n: gsang sngags, 'secret mantra', the tantric way (Sanskrit mantra), and its practitioner rnal 'byor pa, 'yogin'. tha ma'i yang tha ma, 'the last of the last, the lowest of the low'. yin na yang, 'even if he is'. mthong ma thag tu, 'as soon as he sees': ma thag tu, 'without interval', after a verb. sngar 'dris kyi mi, 'a person known before' ('dris, 'to be familiar'). yi dam, 'yidam', the deity one has taken as one's own in practice. yin par ngo shes, 'recognises that they are'. yid ches te, 'trusting, and'. gnyis su med par thim, 'dissolves without being two'. sangs rgyas par 'gyur ro, 'will become a buddha'. The other recension words this sentence a little differently; the print is followed.

sentences.w: དེ་ ཡང་ མི་ཡུལ་དུ་ ཁྲག་འཐུང་ གི་ སྐུ་ འདི་ རྣམས་ མངོན་རྟོགས་ སྒོམས་པ་ དང་༔ མཆོད་བསྟོད་ བྱས་པ་ དང་༔ ཐ་ན་ སྐུ་གཟུགས་ རིས་སུ་ བྲིས་པ་ དང་༔ འབུར་དུ་ དོད་པ་ ལ་སོགས་ མཐོང་བ་ ཁོ་ནས་ ཀྱང་༔ འདིར་ སྐུ་གཟུགས་ ཤར་བ་ དང་ ངོ་ ཤེས་ ནས་ གྲོལ་བ་ ཐོབ་པའི་ གནད་ ཀྱང་ དེ་ལྟར་ ཡིན་ནོ༔
sentences.l: That also: human-world-in, blood-drinkers' forms these (plural), clear-realisation meditated and; offering-praise done and; even body-images picture-as drawn and; relief-as raised and-so-on seen only-by also: here body-images dawned with face knowing, then, freedom obtaining's key-point also thus is.
sentences.i: This is how it works: in the human world one has meditated on these blood-drinking deities in their sādhanas, made them offerings and praises, or even only seen their images painted or moulded in relief, and by that alone, when the images dawn here, one recognises them and is freed. That is the key point.
sentences.n: mngon rtogs, 'clear realisation', the text that describes a deity for meditation (sādhana); sgoms pa, 'meditated', is the print's spelling, here, of bsgoms pa, the past of sgom. mchod bstod, 'offering and praise'. tha na, 'even, at the least'. sku gzugs, 'form, image' of a deity; ris su bris pa, 'drawn as a picture'; 'bur du dod pa, 'standing out in relief' ('bur, 'raised'; dod, 'to stick out'), carved or moulded. mthong ba kho nas, 'by merely seeing' (kho na, 'only'). shar ba dang ngo shes, 'recognising, as they dawn': dang joins the dawning and the knowing. gnad, 'vital point, key'. The print runs pa'i and gnad together across the page join, here divided.

sentences.w: ཡང་ མི་ཡུལ་དུ་ འདུལ་བ་ འཛིན་པའི་ མཁན་པོ་ དང་༔ མཚན་ཉིད་ ཀྱི་ སྟོན་པའི་ ཆོས་སྤྱོད་ ལ་ ཇི་ལྟར་ བརྩོན་ ཞིང་༔ བཤད་པའི་ ཆོས་ ལ་ ཇི་ལྟར་ མཁས་ ཀྱང་༔ གྲོངས་པའི་ ཚེ་ ན༔ གདུང་ དང་༔ རིང་སྲེལ་ དང་༔ འཇའ་འོད་ ལ་སོགས་པའི་ རྟགས་ མི་ འབྱོན་ ཏེ༔
sentences.l: Again, human-world-in, discipline holding's abbots and; characteristics' teachers' dharma-practice in however diligent and, explanation's dharma in however learned though: died's time-at: bone-relics and; pearl-relics and; rainbow-light and-so-on's signs not come-forth, and:
sentences.i: Again, however diligent in religious practice the abbots who hold the discipline and the teachers of philosophy may be in the human world, and however learned in the teaching of explanation, when they die no signs appear, no bone relics, no pearl relics, no rainbow light.
sentences.n: ji ltar ... kyang, 'however ... though'. chos spyod, 'religious practice'; the print has ston pa'i chos spyod, 'the practice of the teachers', where the sense is the same. brtson, 'to be diligent'; bshad pa'i chos, 'the teaching of explanation', learning by commentary. grongs, the respectful 'die'. The signs are those said to appear at a holy person's death: gdung, the respectful word for 'bones', bone relics left after cremation; ring srel, small pearl-like relics found among the ashes, the print's spelling here of ring bsrel (it writes ring bsrel on the next pages); 'ja' 'od, 'rainbow light'. The print runs ring and srel together (རིངསྲེལ), here divided. mi 'byon, 'do not come forth', 'byon, the respectful 'come'.

sentences.w: དེ་ ནི་ གསོན་པོའི་ དུས་སུ་ གསང་སྔགས་ བློར་ མ་ ཤོང་ དང་༔ གསང་སྔགས་ ལ་ གཤེ་སྐུར་ བཏབ་པ་ དང་༔ གསང་སྔགས་ ཀྱི་ ལྷ་ཚོགས་ རྣམས་ རྒྱུས་ མེད་པའི་ དབང་ གིས་ བར་དོར་ ཤར་ ཡང་ ངོ་ མ་ ཤེས་ ཏེ༔
sentences.l: That, as-for: alive's time-at, secret-mantra into-mind not fitted and; secret-mantra at reviling-disparaging cast and; secret-mantra's deity-hosts (plural) acquaintance without's power-by, in-the-between dawned though, face not know, and:
sentences.i: That is because in their lifetime the secret mantra found no room in their minds, they reviled and disparaged it, and they had no acquaintance with its deities; so when those deities dawn in the bardo, they do not recognise them.
sentences.n: blor ma shong, 'did not fit into the mind' (blo, 'mind', with -r): they could not accept it; the print joins shong and dang with no tsheg between them. gshe skur, 'reviling and disparaging' (gshe, 'to revile'; skur, 'to disparage'), with btab pa, the past of 'debs, 'to cast', the verb such words take. rgyus med, 'having no acquaintance with' (rgyus, 'knowledge of a thing'). dbang gis, 'by the force of'. The print writes the -ms of rnams as one sign (རྣམྶ), here written out.

sentences.w: སྔར་ མ་ མཐོང་བ་ གློ་བུར་དུ་ མཐོང་བ་ དེ་ དགྲར་ སོང་ ནས༔ དེ་ ལ་ སྡང་སེམས་ སྐྱེས་ ནས་ དེས་ རྐྱེན་ བྱས་ ངན་སོང་དུ་ འགྲོ་བས༔
sentences.l: Before not seen, suddenly seen, that, into-enemy gone, then: that at hatred-mind arisen, then, that-by condition made, bad-destinies-to going-because:
sentences.i: What they had never seen before, now suddenly seen, turns into an enemy; hatred arises against it, and with that as the cause they go to the lower realms.
sentences.n: glo bur du, 'suddenly'. dgrar song, 'became an enemy': dgra, 'enemy', with -r, 'into', and song, the past stem of 'gro, 'to go'. sdang sems, 'a mind of hatred'. des[?] rkyen byas, 'it made the condition', with that as the cause: on the image the stack looks like ས with no gi-gu, so des is not sure; the other recension has de'i, 'its condition', with the same sense. 'gro bas, 'because they go', runs on into the next sentence.

sentences.w: དེའི་ ཕྱིར་ འདུལ་བ་ འཛིན་པ་ དང་༔ མཚན་ཉིད་པ་ ཇི་ལྟར་ བཟང་ ཡང་༔ ནང་ ནས་ གསང་སྔགས་ ཀྱི་ ཉམས་ལེན་ མེད་པས༔ གདུང་ དང་༔ ཤི་རམ་ དང་༔ རིང་བསྲེལ་ དང་༔ འཇའ་འོད་ ལ་སོགས་པའི་ རྟགས་ མི་ འབྱོན་པའི་ མཚན་ཉིད་ དེ་ལྟར་རོ༔
sentences.l: That's because: discipline holders and; philosophers however good though, inside from secret-mantra's practice is-not-because: bone-relics and; śarīra and; pearl-relics and; rainbow-light and-so-on's signs not coming-forth's characteristic thus is.
sentences.i: So however excellent the holders of the discipline and the philosophers may be, they have no inner practice of the secret mantra, and that is why signs such as bone relics, śarīra, pearl relics and rainbow light do not appear for them.
sentences.n: de'i phyir, 'for that reason, therefore'; the other recension has des. The print runs de'i and phyir together, here divided. mtshan nyid pa, 'a philosopher', one who studies the mtshan nyid; mtshan nyid at the end of the sentence is the same word in its plain sense, 'the defining mark, the reason'. nang nas, 'from within': inwardly. nyams len, 'practice, taking into experience'. pas[?], 'because', is not sure on the image and could be nas, 'then'; the sense is the same. shi ram is taken as the print's spelling of sha ri ram (Sanskrit śarīra), relics. de ltar ro, 'is thus', with the ending -o after -r.

sentences.w: གསང་སྔགས་པ་ ཐ་མའི་ ཡང་ ཐ་མ་ གཅིག་ ཡིན་ ནའང་༔ འཕྲལ་དུ་ སྤྱོད་ལམ་ རྩིང་པ་ དང་༔ མི་ བཙུན་པ་ དང་༔ མི་ མཁས་པ་ དང་༔ ཚུལ་ དང་ མི་ མཐུན་པའི་ སྤྱོད་ལམ་ མི་ མཛེས་པ་ ཇི་ལྟར་ འདུག་ ཀྱང་༔ དེས་ གསང་སྔགས་ ཀྱི་ ཆོས་ ཉམས་སུ་བླང་ མ་ ཐུབ་ ན་ ཡང་༔ དེ་ ལ་ ལོག་ལྟ་ མ་ སྐྱེས་པ་ དང་༔ ཐེ་ཚོམ་ མེད་པ་ དང་༔ གསང་སྔགས་ ལ་ མོས་པ་ བྱས་པ་ ཙམ་ ཀྱང་ སྐབས་ འདིར་ གྲོལ་བ་ ཐོབ་པ་ ཡིན་ ཏེ༔
sentences.l: Mantrin lowest's even lowest one is if-even: for-the-moment conduct coarse and; not disciplined and; not learned and; custom with not agreeing's conduct not beautiful, however appears though; him-by secret-mantra's dharma into-experience take not able if even: that toward wrong-view not arisen and; doubt without and; secret-mantra to devotion done merely also, occasion this-at freedom obtaining is, and:
sentences.i: A mantrin, even the lowest of the low, however coarse, undisciplined and unlearned his conduct may seem for the time being, however unseemly and out of keeping with custom, and even if he cannot put the secret mantra into practice, need only have formed no wrong views of it, have no doubt, and have devotion to it, to be freed at this point.
sentences.n: gsang sngags pa, 'mantrin', a follower of the secret mantra, often a lay tantric. na'ang is a contraction of na yang, 'even if'. 'phral du, 'for the moment, outwardly'. spyod lam, 'conduct, behaviour'; rtsing pa, 'coarse'; mi btsun pa, 'undisciplined, undignified' (btsun pa, 'disciplined, reverend'); tshul dang mi mthun pa, 'not in agreement with propriety'. ji ltar 'dug kyang, 'however it may seem'. des, 'by him', marks the doer of blang, 'to take', the future stem of len: nyams su blang ma thub, 'could not put into practice'. log lta, 'wrong view'; the tshom, 'doubt'; mos pa, 'devotion'. tsam kyang, 'even merely'. The print runs yin and te together at the line join, here divided.

sentences.w: མི་ཡུལ་དུ་ སྤྱོད་ལམ་ མ་ མཛེས་ ཀྱང་ འཆི་བའི་ ཚེ་ ན༔ གདུང་ དང་ རིང་བསྲེལ་ དང་༔ སྐུ་གཟུགས་ དང་༔ འཇའ་འོད་ ལ་སོགས་པའི་ རྟགས་ སྣ་རེ་ ཅིས་ཀྱང་ འབྱུང་བར་ འགྱུར་ ཏེ༔
sentences.l: Human-world-in conduct not beautiful though, dying's time-at: bone-relics and pearl-relics and; images and; rainbow-light and-so-on's signs one-kind-or-another by-all-means arising-into turns, and:
sentences.i: Though his conduct in the human world was unseemly, when he dies some sign or other is sure to appear, bone relics, pearl relics, images, rainbow light and the like,
sentences.n: ma mdzes, 'was not seemly', with ma, the 'not' of the past. sku gzugs, 'images', here among the relics: forms of deities said to appear in the bones or ashes; the text does not explain them. sna re, 'one kind or another'; cis kyang, 'by all means, surely'. 'byung bar 'gyur, 'will come to arise'.

sentences.w: དེས་ན་ གསང་སྔགས་ འདི་ བྱིན་རླབས་ ཤིན་ཏུ་ ཆེ་བའི་ ཕྱིར་རོ༔
sentences.l: Therefore: secret-mantra this, blessing very great's because.
sentences.i: for this secret mantra is of very great blessing.
sentences.n: des na, 'so, thus', here gives the reason for what was just said, and phyir ro, 'it is because', closes it, with the ending -o after -r. byin rlabs, 'blessing' (byin, 'splendour'; rlabs, 'wave'), the power that comes from the buddhas.

sentences.w: གསང་སྔགས་ ཀྱི་ རྣལ་འབྱོར་པ་ འབྲིང་ ཡན་ཆད༔ བསྐྱེད་རྫོགས་ བསྒོམས་པ་ དང་༔ སྙིང་པོ་ བཟླས་པ་ ལ་སོགས་པ་ ཉམས་སུ་བླངས་པ་ རྣམས་ ནི་ ཆོས་ཉིད་ བར་དོ་ འདི་ ཙམ་དུ་ མར་ འཁྱམས་ མི་ དགོས་ ཏེ༔
sentences.l: Secret-mantra's yogins middling and-above: generation-completion meditated and; heart-essence recited and-so-on into-experience taken (plural), as-for: reality-itself between this as-far-as down wander not need, and:
sentences.i: Yogins of the secret mantra of middling ability and above, who have practised the stages of generation and completion, recited the heart mantras and the like, need not wander down as far as this bardo of reality:
sentences.n: 'bring yan chad, 'the middling and above'. bskyed rdzogs, 'generation and completion', the two stages of tantric meditation, building up the deity and dissolving it; bsgoms pa, 'meditated', the past of sgom. snying po, 'essence', the heart mantra of a deity; bzlas, 'to recite', the past stem of zlo. 'di tsam du mar, 'down as far as this' (tsam du, 'as far as'; mar, 'down'). 'khyams mi dgos, 'need not wander'. The print writes the -gs of dgos as one sign (དགོྶ), here written out.

sentences.w: དབུགས་ ཆད་ མ་ཁད་དུ་ རིག་འཛིན་ དང་ དཔའ་བོ་ མཁའ་འགྲོ་ ལ་སོགས་པས་ དག་པ་ མཁའ་སྤྱོད་དུ་ ངེས་པར་ གདན་དྲངས་པར་ འགྱུར་ ཏེ༔
sentences.l: Breath cut just-before: knowledge-holders and heroes, sky-goers and-so-on-by, pure Sky-Faring-to certainly invited-into turn, and:
sentences.i: as their breath stops, the knowledge-holders, heroes, sky-goers and others are sure to come and escort them to the pure Sky-Faring realm.
sentences.n: dbugs chad, 'the breath is cut'; ma khad du, 'just before, at the point of'. la sogs pas, 'by ... and the rest'. gdan drangs, 'to invite, to escort', the respectful word for leading someone (gdan, 'seat'; drangs, the past stem of 'dren, 'to lead'). dag pa mkha' spyod, 'the pure Sky-Faring realm', as in 008.

sentences.w: དེའི་ རྟགས་སུ་ ནམ་མཁའ་ གཡའ་ དག་པ་ དང་༔ འཇའ་ དང་ འོད་དུ་ ཐིམ་པ་ དང་༔ མེ་ཏོག་ གི་ ཆར་ དང་༔ སྤོས་ ཀྱི་ དྲི་ དང་༔ ནམ་མཁའ་ ལ་ རོལ་མོར་ སྒྲ་ ཟེར་ དང༔ གདུང་ དང་ རིང་བསྲེལ་ དང་༔ སྐུ་གཟུགས་ ལ་སོགས་པ་ བྱོན་པ་ ནི་ དེའི་ རྟགས་ ཡིན་ནོ༔
sentences.l: That's sign-as: sky haze-pure and; rainbow and light-into dissolving and; flowers' rain and; incense's scent and; sky-in music-as(?) sound, rays(?) and; bone-relics and pearl-relics and; images and-so-on come-forth, as-for, that's sign is.
sentences.i: As signs of it, the sky is clear and without haze, there is dissolving into rainbow and light, a rain of flowers, the scent of incense, music and rays of light in the sky, and bone relics, pearl relics, images and the like appear: these are its signs.
sentences.n: The print has ནམ་མཁར (nam mkhar), a misprint for ནམ་མཁའ (nam mkha'), corrected here: the letter is clearly the open ར, set beside the closed འ of mkha' earlier in the same line, and nam mkha', 'sky', is the only word. rtags[?] su: the print writes rtag at the line end, squeezed against the frame and not sure, with su on the next line; rtags su, 'as a sign', is written out. g.ya' dag pa, 'clean of haze' (g.ya', 'haze, tarnish'). 'ja' dang 'od du thim pa, 'dissolving into rainbow and light': who or what dissolves is not said. me tog gi char, 'a rain of flowers'; spos kyi dri, 'the scent of incense'. rol mor sgra is kept as printed: rol mo is 'music', and rol mor, 'as music', is awkward; the other recension has rol mo'i, 'of music'. The print may have ར for འ here as in mkhar, but rol mo'i would also need a gi-gu, so it is not corrected; the sense is taken as 'the sound of music'. zer[?], 'rays', is very doubtful: one tall stack stands at the line end with no clear vowel, and is read zer because the other recension has sgra dang zer dang, 'sounds and rays'; the print has no dang after sgra. The print also has a stray tsheg in dang across the line join (ད་ང), here removed. byon pa, 'having come forth', the respectful past.

sentences.w: དེའི་ ཕྱིར་ འདུལ་བ་ འཛིན་པ་ དང་༔ མཚན་ཉིད་པ་ དང་༔ དམ་ཚིག་ ཉམས་པའི་ སྔགས་པ་ དང་༔ སྐྱེ་བོ་ ཐ་མལ་པ་ ཐམས་ཅད་ ལ་ ནི༔ ཐོས་གྲོལ་ ཆེན་མོ་ འདི་ མེད་པའི་ ཐབས་ མེད་དོ༔
sentences.l: That's because: discipline holders and; philosophers and; commitment broken's mantrins and; people ordinary all for, as-for: Hearing-Liberation Great this without's means is-not.
sentences.i: Therefore for the holders of the discipline, for philosophers, for mantrins whose commitments are broken, and for all ordinary people, there is no doing without this Great Liberation through Hearing.
sentences.n: dam tshig nyams pa'i sngags pa, 'a mantrin whose commitments (dam tshig, Sanskrit samaya) are broken'. X med pa'i thabs med, 'there is no way of being without X': it cannot be done without. The print runs dam and tshig together across the page join and its opening ornament, here divided. This line, 89.1, is a short one, closed by an empty framed box.

sentences.w: རྫོགས་ཆེན་པ་ དང་༔ ཕྱག་རྒྱ་ཆེན་པོ་ ལ་སོགས་པ་ བསྒོམ་པའི་ སྒོམ་ཆེན་ དག་ ནི་ འཆི་ཁའི་ བར་དོར་ འོད་གསལ་ ངོས་ ཟིན་ ནས་ ཆོས་སྐུ་ ཐོབ་པར་ འགྱུར་བས༔ ཐོས་གྲོལ་ འདི་ ཀློག་ མི་ དགོས་པ་ ཤ་སྟག་ འོང་ངོ་༔
sentences.l: Great-Perfection-practitioners and; Great-Seal and-so-on meditating's great-meditators (plural), as-for: death-point's in-the-between clear-light recognition caught, then, body-of-truth obtaining-into turn-because: Hearing-Liberation this reading not needing, nothing-but come.
sentences.i: Great meditators who practise the Great Perfection, the Great Seal and the like recognise the clear light in the bardo of the moment of death and attain the body of truth, so they all, without exception, have no need of this Liberation through Hearing being read.
sentences.n: rdzogs chen, 'great perfection' (Dzogchen), the highest teaching of the Nyingma school, and rdzogs chen pa, one who practises it; phyag rgya chen po, 'the Great Seal' (008). sgom chen, 'great meditator', a meditator who has given his life to it; dag, plural. chos sku thob par 'gyur bas, 'because they come to attain the body of truth'; the print runs 'gyur and bas together at the line join, here divided. klog, 'to read (aloud)', stands for the more usual klag, and the print has thos grol 'di without chen mo, where the other recension has thos grol chen mo 'di. sha stag, 'nothing but, every one' (008); 'ong ngo, 'they come to be'.

sentences.w: དེ་ ཡང་ འཆི་ཁའི་ བར་དོར་ ངོས་ ཟིན་ ནས་ ཆོས་སྐུ་ ཐོབ་བོ༔
sentences.l: That also: death-point's in-the-between recognition caught, then, body-of-truth obtain.
sentences.i: That is, recognising in the bardo of the moment of death, they attain the body of truth.
sentences.n: This and the next two sentences set the three bardos against the three bodies of a buddha (the homage of the pilot): the bardo of the moment of death and the body of truth, the bardo of reality and the body of perfect enjoyment, the bardo of becoming and the body of emanation. thob bo, 'attain', with the ending -o after -b.

sentences.w: ཆོས་ཉིད་ བར་དོ་ འདིར་ ཞི་ཁྲོའི་ སྣང་བ་ འཆར་བའི་ སྐབས་སུ༔ ངོས་ ཟིན་ ནས་ ལོངས་སྤྱོད་ རྫོགས་པའི་ སྐུ་ ཐོབ་བོ༔
sentences.l: Reality-itself between this-in(?): peaceful-wrathful-ones' appearances dawning's occasion-at, recognition caught, then, enjoyment perfect's body obtain.
sentences.i: Here in the bardo of reality, when the appearances of the peaceful and wrathful deities dawn, those who recognise them attain the body of perfect enjoyment.
sentences.n: 'dir[?], 'here in', is doubtful: the image shows, after do, a box-like letter, a letter with gi-gu and a ra-like letter, read as 'dir; the other recension has bar dor, 'in the bardo', and the sense is the same. Whether the print has a tsheg between do and 'dir is not seen. zhi khro, 'the peaceful and wrathful (deities)'. longs spyod rdzogs pa'i sku, 'the body of perfect enjoyment', written out in full where the pilot had longs spyod rdzogs sku.

sentences.w: སྲིད་པའི་ བར་དོར་ ངོས་ ཟིན་ ནས་ སྤྲུལ་སྐུ་ ཐོབ་པ་ དང༔ གཞན་ དག་ ཀས་ མཐོ་རིས་སུ་ སྐྱེ་བ་ སྟེ༔ ཆོས་ འདི་ དང་ འཕྲད་ ནས་ སྐྱེ་བ་ ཕྱི་མ་ ཆགས་ ལ་ སྤྱོད་པའི་ ལས་འཕྲོ་ ཡོད་པས༔
sentences.l: Becoming's in-the-between recognition caught, then, emanation-body obtaining and; others (plural) by(?) high-realms-in being-born, and: teaching this with met, then, birth later formed(?) and practising's karmic-residue there-is-because:
sentences.i: In the bardo of becoming, those who recognise attain the body of emanation; and others are born in the higher realms, because, having met this teaching, they have the karmic residue to practise it in a later birth.
sentences.n: srid pa'i bar do, 'the bardo of becoming', in which a new birth is sought; it is the subject of text ja. sprul sku, 'the body of emanation'. gzhan dag kas[?] is a phrase the other recension does not have, and two of its letters are doubtful: gzhan dag, 'others', is clear, then a ka and a sa-like letter crushed against the frame. A word such as gzhan dag kyang, 'others, too', would fit the sense, but no ya-btags or nga is seen, so the letters stand as read; kas is taken as the -s that marks who is born, and the reading is uncertain. mtho ris, 'the high realms', the births of gods and humans. chags[?] is doubtful and is another word not in the other recension: chags is 'to come into being, take shape' (also 'to be attached'), and the phrase is taken as 'when the later birth takes shape, to practise'; the sense of chags la here is not sure. las 'phro, 'karmic residue', as in the parts before. The print adds this second group, 'others', who are born in the higher realms, to the three bodies; the other recension has only the three. The print has no tsheg before the ༔ of dang.

sentences.w: དེའི་ ཕྱིར་ ཐོས་གྲོལ་ ཆེན་མོ་ འདི་ ནི་ མ་ བསྒོམ་པར་ སངས་རྒྱས་པའི་ ཆོས་ ཐོས་པ་ ཙམ་ གྱིས་ གྲོལ་བ་ ཐོབ་པའི་ ཆོས༔ སྡིག་པོ་ཆེ་ གསང་ལམ་ ལ་ འཁྲིད་པའི་ ཆོས༔ སྐད་ཅིག་ གཅིག་ གིས་ བྱེ་བྲག་ ཕྱེད་པའི་ ཆོས༔ སྐད་ཅིག་ གཅིག་ གིས་ རྫོགས་སངས་རྒྱས་པའི་ ཆོས་ ཟབ་མོ་ ཡིན་ ཏེ༔
sentences.l: That's because: Hearing-Liberation Great this, as-for: not meditating-ly buddha-becoming's teaching, hearing merely by freedom obtaining's teaching; great-wrongdoers secret-path onto leading's teaching; instant one by distinction dividing's teaching; instant one by perfect-buddha-becoming's teaching profound is, and:
sentences.i: Therefore this Great Liberation through Hearing is the teaching by which one becomes a buddha without meditating, the teaching that frees by hearing alone, the teaching that leads great wrongdoers onto the secret path, the teaching that makes the difference in a single instant, the profound teaching by which one becomes a perfect buddha in a single instant;
sentences.n: A list of names for the teaching, each ending in chos, 'teaching', with ༔ after each but the first; without that ༔ the first two could also be read as one, 'the teaching by which one is freed merely by hearing the teaching of becoming a buddha without meditating'. ma bsgom par, 'without meditating' (bsgom, the future stem of sgom); sangs[?] is blotted on the image, though sangs rgyas, 'buddha', is not in doubt. thos pa tsam gyis, 'by merely hearing'. sdig po che, 'great wrongdoer'; gsang lam, 'the secret path', where the other recension has gseb lam, 'the hidden path'; 'khrid, 'to lead'. skad cig gcig gis, 'in a single instant'. bye brag phyed, 'to divide the difference', to make the decisive distinction, between saṃsāra and freedom. rdzogs sangs rgyas, 'perfectly awakened'. The print runs par and sangs together across the page join, and pa'i and chos at the next line join; both are divided here.

sentences.w: འདིས་ སླེབ་པའི་ སེམས་ཅན་ ངན་སོང་དུ་ སོང་བ་ མི་ སྲིད་དོ༔
sentences.l: This-by reached's beings, bad-destinies-to gone, not possible.
sentences.i: no being whom it has reached can go to the lower realms.
sentences.n: 'dis, 'by this', with the -s that marks the doer. sleb pa'i sems can, 'the beings reached': sleb, 'to arrive, reach', the beings to whom the teaching comes. song ba, 'having gone'. mi srid do, 'it is not possible'. The next part begins on the same line, with 'di dang.
